'''''Agave utahensis''''' is a species of [[agave]] known by the common name '''Utah agave'''.<ref name="iucn status 20 November 2021" />

Varieties of the species include the '''Nevada agave''' and '''Kaibab agave'''.

It is an uncommon plant of the United States' desert southwest, in the states of [[Utah]], [[Nevada]], [[Arizona]], and [[California]]. Although plants in some areas are threatened, overall the species is stable and is considered to be of [[Least Concern]] by the [[IUCN]].<ref name="iucn status 20 November 2021" />

==Description==
''Agave utahensis'' is a rosette-shaped agave having blue-green sharp-spiked leaves.

The [[raceme]] inflorescence is very tall, reaching a maximum of 4 m (12 ft). It is generally yellow or yellow-green with bulbous yellow flowers. The fruits are capsules 1 to 3 centimeters long and containing black seed.

Agave utahensis can grow in [[clonal colony|clonal colonies]]; a 2024 survey conducted in Nevada estimated that some colonies are more than 150 years old.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Zarrella |first1=Dan |title=Agave utahensis Clonal Rings: Artifacts of Indigenous Resource Management |journal=Cactus and Succulent Journal |date=29 November 2024 |volume=96 |issue=4 |pages=343–359 |doi=10.2985/015.096.0406 |url=https://bioone.org/journals/cactus-and-succulent-journal/volume-96/issue-4/015.096.0406/Agave-utahensis-Clonal-Rings-Artifacts-of-Indigenous-Resource-Management/10.2985/015.096.0406.short |access-date=16 December 2024|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Uses==
''Agave utahensis'' is cultivated as an ornamental plant. In the UK it has won the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/694/Agave-utahensis/Details | title = ''Agave utahensis''
| website = www.rhs.org | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 27 February 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = November 2018 | page = 3 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | website = www.rhs.org | access-date = 27 February 2020}}</ref>

The plant was used for food and fiber by local Native American peoples such as the [[Havasupai]]. Among the [[Navajo people|Navajo]], the plant is used to make blankets.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://herb.umd.umich.edu/herb/search.pl?searchstring=Agave+utahensis|title=BRIT - Native American Ethnobotany Database}}</ref>
